articles.headline: Kirk Cousins says call with Kevin O'Connell convinced him to OK Vikings trade
articles.description: Kirk Cousins has rejoined the Vikings after not quite three years away, relishing his familiarity with the Twin Cities area, the people in the organization.
articles.headlineJa: カーク・カズンズ、ケビン・オコネルとの電話がバイキングスへの移籍を承諾する決め手になったと語る
articles.descriptionJa: カーク・カズンズが約3年ぶりにバイキングスに復帰。ツインシティーズ周辺の環境や、組織のメンバーとの親しみやすさを喜んでいる。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- If he were going to be traded this season, Kirk Cousins had one condition.

"I'm not too interested in completely starting over," the quarterback said Wednesday upon arriving in the Minnesota Vikings' practice facility to begin his second tenure with the team.

Cousins, who played for the Vikings from 2018-23 and is now 38 years old, said that a telephone conversation Tuesday afternoon with coach Kevin O'Connell convinced him to accept a trade from the Las Vegas Raiders. In exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick, the Vikings got a new starting quarterback with familiarity in their offensive system and a chance to elevate the team's season-long offensive doldrums. This will mark the third time Cousins and O'Connell have worked together, including O'Connell's tenure with the Washington Commanders as their quarterbacks coach.

"Kevin knows me," Cousins said. "Kevin knows what I do well. Kevin knows what I don't do well. Kevin knows what I can handle. Kevin knows what I can't handle. And I think that helps, not just that he knows your strengths, but that he knows your weaknesses and that as a result he's going to try to protect you and not have you do things that he knows, 'You know what, that's not how Kirk functions. That's not his best chance of success.' And I think the fact that he knows me well, the good about me and the bad about me. I think should help us."

O'Connell stopped short of confirming that Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, saying: "That's what we're working towards, but also want to be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it."

Week 1 starter Kyler Murray remains sidelined by a strained hamstring and backup Carson Wentz (ankle) was projected to be limited if the Vikings had held a practice.

Speaking about Cousins in Green Bay, Packers coach Matt LaFleur said: "Yeah. He'll be out there. He'll be starting. I'm fairly confident of that."

O'Connell did not immediately commit to Wentz backing up Cousins, noting that No. 3 quarterback Max Brosmer's "growth and development is ongoing." Murray will serve as Cousins' backup when he is healthy, O'Conell said.

"I believe in Kyler," O'Connell said. "just like I believe in Carson. I believe in Max. I want him to get healthy and get back to work because you just never know. We do not hold the cards on how this will go from a health standpoint or anything like that with anybody on our team."

Although the Vikings did not practice Wednesday, Cousins spent Wednesday morning with O'Connell, reviewing the offensive scheme and having initial game plan discussions. Having lost consecutive games following a 6-0 start, the Vikings know they will have to elevate their offense to ensure a playoff spot and then make a run to the Super Bowl.

Through Week 9, the Vikings have the NFL's second-worst offense based on expected points added (EPA).

articles.headline: Curry confronts critics over comments about wife Ayesha
articles.description: Warriors star Stephen Curry took to social media Wednesday to address criticisms made of wife Ayesha's acting role in "Second Chance Holiday."
articles.headlineJa: カリー、妻アイシャへのコメントに関する批判に反論
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのスター、ステフィン・カリーは水曜日、妻アイシャの「Second Chance Holiday」での演技に対する批判に対処するため、ソーシャルメディア上で発言した。
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry took to social media Wednesday to address criticisms made of the acting role his wife, Ayesha, has in "Second Chance Holiday."

Former NBA players Nick Young -- who won a ring with Steph in 2017-18 -- and Gilbert Arenas reacted to the topic of Ayesha's kissing scene on the "We Said What We Said" podcast Saturday.

"The only blemish in the family is the wife in the sense because she doesn't act like the other superstars' wives. [Michael] Jordan's wife, Cookie [Johnson], that's Magic's [Johnson's] wife, Savannah [James], right, where we don't want to hear you," Arenas said on the podcast. "She hasn't been the American wife that the public knows."

Arenas went further, saying they "want" Ayesha's kissing scene to be a problem because "Steph is so innocent."

"I've been hearing a lot of noise and usually the noise doesn't bother me, doesn't bother Ayesha but, this one in particular when you try to step on the accomplishments of my wife and you know, obviously, leading podcast tapings and topics, giving opinions on somebody else's wife," Steph said, "Nick, Gil, Emmanuel [Acho] and anybody else who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you really don't know about.

"Something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do, even the ignorance behind how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this off but something needs to be said."

Ayesha comes from an acting background that includes appearances in several films, such as "Irish Wish" and "Joy to the World," and the TV show "Hannah Montana" in her early career.

"Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, I'd kindly suggest you just give the happy hands, the congratulations and maybe the apology as loud as you lead your shows with this topic," Steph said. "Appreciate the free pub."

Shortly after Steph addressed Arenas and Young's comments on social media, the duo issued an apology on "Gil's Arena."

"I'm sorry Steph. You my dog, I love you. If I say anything, I apologize like a man," Young said.

"I'm sorry if he's offended. I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying he's such a perfect dude," Arenas said.

"Second Chance Holiday" premiered on the Roku channel Thursday.

articles.headline: Cardinals to start rookie QB Carson Beck against Rams
articles.description: The Cardinals will start their third quarterback in three weeks, with rookie Carson Beck getting the nod for Sunday's home game against the Rams.
articles.headlineJa: カージナルス、ラムス戦で新人QBカーソン・ベックを先発起用へ
articles.descriptionJa: カージナルスは3週間で3人目のクォーターバックを起用することになり、日曜日のラムスとのホームゲームでは新人カーソン・ベックが先発を務める。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his NFL debut Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams, coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday.

Quarterback Gardner Minshew II was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after suffering a UCL injury in his throwing arm Sunday at Seattle, paving the way for Beck to get his first career start.

Beck, a third-round pick by Arizona, spent the first eight weeks as the Cardinals' emergency third quarterback and was inactive on game day. He was the backup against the Seahawks after Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore. 

LaFleur said Beck, who played in 55 games over six seasons at Georgia and Miami, won't be fazed by the moment. Beck's last start came in January in the CFP National Championship Game, which Miami lost to Indiana 27-21. The game before, Beck led the Hurricanes to a win over Ole Miss in the CFP quarterfinals at the Fiesta Bowl at State Farm Stadium, where he'll play Sunday.

"I know this isn't too big for him," LaFleur said. "Go have some fun, man. Go let it sling."

LaFleur said he wants to see Beck continue what he has been doing in practice and treat each play individually.

"You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday, but just the way he goes about his business ... have all the confidence that he's ready to roll," the coach said. 

LaFleur said Beck "will not be scared" of letting it fly in his NFL debut. As the backup, Beck doubled his workload running the scout team offense, according to quarterbacks coach Matt Schaub.

"He can translate those into getting himself prepared, moving around the pocket, not just going through the motions, and he's really diligent on that and just going through his process, which he's been doing all year, but it's just those physical reps," Schaub said.

Schaub said he saw a change in Beck's demeanor with the increased reps.

"He's a confident kid by nature, so he's reserved, but I mean he's been what he's been since he's been here," Schaub said. "And so it's been good to see him getting his workload ramped up, especially he had some little injury situation in camp, so he lost some reps and some experience and just development there, but he's picked back up and so we like where he's at."

LaFleur credited Beck's college experience for helping him prepare to start. 

"He's been a pro since he's been here," LaFleur said. "He puts in the exact amount of work that he needs. And then from a physical standpoint, he'll obviously get 100% of the reps."

Beck will be throwing to a number of familiar receivers he worked with on the practice squad before he was the No. 2 quarterback last week. Arizona's currently active receiving corps of Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil and Devin Duvernay has a combined eight catches this season. However, Beck's tight end corps of Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano has 94 combined.

LaFleur said playing in his first NFL game with receivers he knows well will be beneficial to Beck.

articles.headline: Donovan Mitchell details Coco Jones wedding, music passion on 'The Tonight Show'
articles.description: The Cavs guard revealed wedding details and a new hobby in his appearance on "The Tonight Show."
articles.headlineJa: ドノバン・ミッチェル、「ザ・トゥナイト・ショー」でココ・ジョーンズとの結婚式や音楽への情熱を語る
articles.descriptionJa: キャブスのガードは、「ザ・トゥナイト・ショー」への出演の中で、結婚式の詳細や新しい趣味について明かした。
articles.body:
It's no coincidence Donovan Mitchell is married to R&B singer-songwriter Coco Jones. They share the language they both love: music.

On Tuesday night, the Cleveland Cavaliers star guard appeared as a guest on "The Tonight Show" with Jimmy Fallon, where he spoke about being married to the Grammy Award-winning artist.

The couple tied the knot back in August. Mitchell, who proposed to the singer in July 2025, says he "planned" the music for the wedding and joked about his idea of planning the ceremony before going into detail about how their big day was set up.

"We had two tents. She wanted a real intimate ceremony, and I was like 'I'm inviting my third grade teacher; I'm inviting everybody,'" Mitchell said.

In one tent, Mitchell says there were around 40 people for an intimate ceremony. Once attendees walked out to the left, he describes, there was a bigger tent dedicated to the wedding reception.

"That was my part of the wedding," Mitchell jokes.

What began as a conversation between Mitchell and Fallon quickly transitioned into the Cavs guard's love for music. And from what the couple danced to at their wedding -- Musiq Soulchild's "Love" -- he's got immaculate music taste.

Mitchell then shared a bit about his musical background, which consisted of him playing the drums before he ever set foot on an NBA court. He said he started playing drums in the fourth grade, with his inspiration stemming from his mom having pots and pans and him banging on the dishes to produce sound.

"I told [Questlove] I'm coming for your job soon," Mitchell said, prompting the six-time Grammy Award winner -- who anchors Fallon's house band, The Roots -- to hold up his drumsticks in a joking fashion.

Mitchell revealed that he recently got into DJing since Jones gave him a DJ controller board. He recalled going back to his alma mater, Louisville, and performing a two-hour set off the top.

"Everybody loved it," Mitchell said.

The guard is averaging 22.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists in the 2026-27 regular season, but in his downtime, music could be a calming point for the seven-time All-Star.

articles.headline: New Bills safety Amani Hooker will be 'ready to go' vs. Jets
articles.description: Amani Cooper said he's confident he'll be able to pick up defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's scheme by kickoff vs. the Jets.
articles.headlineJa: ビルズの新加入セーフティ、アマニ・フッカーがジェッツ戦に向けて「準備万端」
articles.descriptionJa: アマニ・クーパーは、ジェッツ戦のキックオフまでにディフェンシブ・コーディネーター、ジム・レオンハードの戦術を習得できると自信を語った。
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Newly acquired Bills safety Amani Hooker is adamant he'll make his debut Sunday at the Jets.

The Bills acquired Hooker and a fifth-round draft pick from the Titans in the final hours before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, sending a second-rounder to Tennessee in return.

Hooker, who has an NFL-best five interceptions this season, arrived in Buffalo late Tuesday and was on the field for the Bills' walkthrough practice Wednesday.

He said he's confident he'll be able to pick up defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's scheme by kickoff vs. the Jets.

"At the end of the day, it's football," he said Wednesday. "Every team runs Cover 4. Every team runs Cover 2 and Cover 3. So it's really just about terminology and what they call different things and how they play certain looks.

"I'm going to play on Sunday. I'll be ready to go."

Hooker joins a Bills secondary ranked 29th in pass defense. Coach Joe Brady said the decision to trade for him was not an indictment of Damar Hamlin, the safety Hooker is expected to replace. But Hooker still arrives in Buffalo amid ongoing concerns about back-end communication and play-making skills.

Whatever concerns exist in Buffalo, it's still a long way from Tennessee.

Hooker trades a 1-7 record with the Titans for a 7-1 mark with the Bills. Reflecting on his final weeks with the Titans - he was named a captain, logged three interceptions against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals, was the subject of trade rumors where the Titans were reportedly unwilling to deal him and then ultimately was traded anyway -- Hooker struck a diplomatic tone.

"It's just negotiation, you know," he said. "They're all talking to teams, very similar in contract negotiations. They're trying get the best for everybody. And I understand the Titans by saying 'Amani Hooker's no go.' But at the end of the day, I'm ready for whatever comes."

Hooker said he was in communication with the Titans' front office while he saw the trade rumors swirling on social media. He said he understands what a general manager's job is and didn't express any frustration or ill will toward the organization with whom he'd spent his first eight pro seasons.

Now, Hooker's looking forward.

"It's amazing," he said. "That's literally all I can say. Because I've been on a team that hasn't been winning. So I'm obviously very grateful for the Titans and what they did for me. But in the past, we haven't been winning. And to be on a team that's putting up points with a quarterback and offensive guys that are on fire, and a great defense, I'm just excited to be here."

articles.headline: Sources: Man United contact U.S. Soccer over Poch; Carrick meeting Thursday
articles.description: Manchester United have made contact with U.S. Soccer ahead of triggering Mauricio Pochettino's $10 million release clause as they close on a deal to hire the USMNT manager to replace Michael Carrick, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると：マンU、ポチェッティーノ獲得に向け米国サッカー協会に接触。カリックとの面会は木曜日
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、マイケル・カリックの後任として米国代表監督のマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを獲得するため、1,000万ドルの契約解除条項を発動する前段階として、米国サッカー協会に接触した。
articles.body:
Manchester United have made contact with U.S. Soccer ahead of triggering Mauricio Pochettino's $10 million release clause as they close on a deal to hire the USMNT manager to replace Michael Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Sources added that executives from Man United are set to meet with Carrick on Thursday -- with the expectation that the 45-year-old will be relieved of his duties -- as the club pushes ahead with plans to hire Pochettino.

It will likely cost United another $2 million to hire Pochettino's staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez.

United executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason WIlcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday ahead of their Thursday meeting with Carrick.

Carrick signed a two-year contract in May, but has overseen a poor start to the season. United have won just one Premier League game -- against newly-promoted Ipswich in August -- and sit 18th in the table.

The club have so far remained tight-lipped about the future of former United star player Carrick, who was at Carrington on Wednesday to lead training with the players not currently on international duty.

Pochettino is preparing for two USMNT games against Haiti, one on Nov. 14 and another on Nov. 17, in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

A source told ESPN that U.S. Soccer said it expects Pochettino to oversee the two games against Haiti, the first for the Americans since winning all four matches during the Sept./Oct. international window.

Pochettino has extensive Premier League experience after spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He was considered for the United job before in 2018, 2022 and 2024.

United's next fixture is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

articles.headline: Sean McVay: Rams optimistic WR Davante Adams will return 'sooner than later'
articles.description: The Rams are optimistic that injured wide receiver Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later," coach Sean McVay said.
articles.headlineJa: ショーン・マクベイ：ラムズ、WRダバンテ・アダムスの復帰は「そう遠くないうちに」と楽観視
articles.descriptionJa: ショーン・マクベイ監督は、負傷しているワイドレシーバーのダバンテ・アダムスが、ハムストリングの怪我から「そう遠くないうちに」復帰することに楽観的な見通しを示している。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- One of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams did not trade for a wide receiver before the NFL trade deadline, coach Sean McVay said, is because Los Angeles is "optimistic" that Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later."

McVay initially said Adams, who ruptured his semitendinosus late in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, was expected to miss six to 10 weeks with the injury. McVay said Wednesday that Adams returning after the Rams host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 is a "realistic timeline for him."

The Rams are currently without wide receiver Puka Nacua, who injured his right knee and toe on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. McVay said Wednesday that the Rams will not place Nacua on injured reserve related to roster mechanics, "but he still is going to be out for an extended period of time."

"It wasn't like any sort of new information," McVay said.

Nacua has 25 catches in his past two games, the second most by a Rams player in the Super Bowl era, according to ESPN Research. The rest of the team has combined for 18 during that span.

The Rams signed wide receiver Xavier Smith to the active roster Tuesday. He spent the first three weeks of the season on the Rams' roster before they cut him. Los Angeles also put wide receiver Jordan Whittington on injured reserve on Tuesday with his back injury.

McVay said the Rams want to make sure they activate tight end Terrance Ferguson from injured reserve before his 21-day clock ends. Ferguson, who injured his ankle in Week 3, returned to practice last week.

On Friday, he injured his hamstring, putting him out "a couple weeks," McVay said. McVay said Wednesday that the Rams' goal is to have a roster spot open for the tight end by the time the window closes, even if he's not ready to play. If the Rams do not activate him by then, he would be on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

The Rams lead the NFL in plays (226) and yards (1,211) with three tight ends on the field, according to ESPN Research. The Rams have the second-most touchdowns in 13 personnel.

articles.body:
Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, while Manchester United's list of defensive options now includes Brentford center back Nathan Collins, while Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The Republic of Ireland captain has a contract until 2029, but 8th-placed Brentford would expect a hefty sum to let him go. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have conceded more Premier League goals this season than the 19 Man United have let in, and Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is also reported to be on the club's shortlist.

- Arsenal are eyeing a January move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to TalkSPORT. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.

- AC Milan are already making a move for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January and want to pair him with Gonçalo Ramos, as reported by Gazzetta dello Sport. The negotiations are likely to be costly, though, as Brugge rejected a €35 million bid from Roma in the summer and Tresoldi has since gone on to score 13 goals in 15 games across the Jupiler Pro League and Champions League. It is expected that a fee of €50 million would now be required to sign the 22-year-old.

articles.headline: Schmeichel blasts Man United's 'disrespectful' treatment of Carrick amid Pochettino links
articles.description: Peter Schmeichel has criticised Manchester United for their "disrespectful" treatment of Michael Carrick as the club continue to be linked with Mauricio Pochettino.
articles.body:
Peter Schmeichel has criticised Manchester United for their "disrespectful" treatment of Michael Carrick as the club continue to be linked with Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino is the leading candidate to replace Carrick as head coach and the club have opened talks with the 54-year-old's representatives, sources also told ESPN.

But former United goalkeeper Schmeichel believes the problems at the club stem from above Carrick, and that the under-pressure boss should get the chance to bring in his own players when the January transfer window opens.

"I absolutely do feel sympathy for him. I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him," Schmeichel told 'The Overlap Daily.'

"If I'm honest, I don't think he's doing anything wrong. I know the team that he's in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don't put all of that on him.

"There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Sir Alex [Ferguson] and David Gill left the club. And it's never been corrected.

"It's not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it's just gone worse.

"And if you think about this transfer window now, it's abundantly clear to everyone -- everyone who knows just a little bit about football -- that Manchester United needed defenders.

"They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender. You can't win games if you concede 30 goals in 10 games ... that was not addressed.

"So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael.

- Man United near Mauricio Pochettino deal, Michael Carrick awaits verdict - sources

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

"I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about ..."

Pochettino enjoyed great success at Tottenham, leading them to the 2019 Champions League final.

One of his star players there, England captain Harry Kane, paid tribute to his former coach on Wednesday.

"Me and Mauricio obviously have a fantastic relationship," he said. "I mentioned him as one of the coaches who had a big impact on my career and definitely my development at that stage in my career.

"I needed his guidance. The way he pushed me, not just on the pitch but off the pitch as well was really, really helpful.

"Obviously a fantastic coach, he's managed the biggest clubs in the world. From my point of view, I can't speak highly enough of him. We'll have to wait and see what happens but I know he's a great guy and also a fantastic manager."

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Jets' Will McDonald has 'earned' bigger role, coach says
articles.description: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Will McDonald IV has "earned" a bigger role after meeting with the pass rusher following his trade request.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets didn't oblige Will McDonald IV's trade request, but they're planning to satisfy his desire for more playing time.

Coach Aaron Glenn, who had a one-hour meeting with the pass rusher Saturday, said Wednesday that McDonald has "earned" a bigger role.

"Obviously, there's some things that he needs to improve on -- I think he's done an outstanding job of doing that -- so I think we all can look forward to seeing his play time improve because of what he's done," Glenn said. "He's earned the right to be able to do that."

Glenn's comments came two days after McDonald's trade request became public. Sources said there was interest in McDonald before Tuesday's trade deadline, but the Jets decided to retain the 2023 first-round pick, who is signed through 2027.

McDonald has been frustrated for weeks, and he's been expressing that sentiment to the coaching staff, a source said. He decided enough was enough after playing only 23 of 65 defensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

"I just want to clear everything up," McDonald said Wednesday. "There's no hard feelings with the coaches and staff or anybody here. I just want to play, and I just want to help the team win."

The Jets (2-7) haven't been winning. They have a four-game losing streak and face the first-place Buffalo Bills (7-1) on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

McDonald was an every-down player last season -- he led the team with eight sacks -- but his role changed this season. The Jets switched to a 3-4 front and added three edge players -- David Bailey (No. 2 overall pick), Kingsley Enagbare and Joseph Ossai, who has played only three games due to injuries.

Glenn said McDonald is a "huge part of what we're doing," but that isn't reflected in his playing time. He has played only 46% of the snaps, mostly on passing downs -- 12th most on defense. He has three sacks, two fumble recoveries and one forced fumble. A natural edge rusher, he has 24.5 sacks in 56 career games.

"Every player wants to get on the field, help the team win, so it's not rocket science," McDonald said. "I don't want to make it a big deal as much as the media is making it, because ultimately the goal is to win and help the team."

McDonald said he will "trust the coaches" to follow through on their promise for more playing time. Listed at 6-foot-4, 245 pounds, he's undersized and isn't strong against the run -- one of the reasons for limited playing time.

"His pass rush, I think we all know, is second to none," Glenn said. "He's been in a lot of those situations where he can't rush passer. It's my job to make sure I put him in position to play more because he's improving."

articles.headline: Man United near Mauricio Pochettino deal, Michael Carrick awaits verdict - sources
articles.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is set to take training again on Wednesday as he waits for news on his future, with the club in contact with Mauricio Pochettino, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester United are nearing an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino while Michael Carrick waits for news on his future, sources have told ESPN.

Pochettino is the leading candidate to replace Carrick and the club have opened talks with the 54-year-old's representatives, sources also told ESPN.

The former Argentina defender signed a new contract with the United States in August, but is known to be keen on taking over at Old Trafford. United are set to approach U.S. Soccer once they have a deal in place with Pochettino, sources told ESPN.

Club executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are meeting minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

The summit is pre-planned, but Carrick's position will dominate the agenda.

Sources have told ESPN that Carrick, who is leading training on Wednesday, is expected to be relieved of his duties following a poor start to the season which has seen United slip into the bottom three of the Premier League.

Club sources insist a final decision has not yet been taken and would first require sign off from both Ratcliffe and majority owners, the Glazer family.

United players not on international duty reported to Carrington on Tuesday for an afternoon training session led by Carrick and his staff.

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

- Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye move for Forest's Murillo

- Man United shouldn't keep Carrick despite Villa comeback

Further sessions are scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday before the players are given time off ahead of their next game against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

U.S. Soccer confirmed planned media access with players scheduled for Wednesday had been cancelled in observance of Veterans Day, which removed the possibility of Pochettino's squad being asked to comment on the news of his potential exit.

Former Bournemouth and Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have also been considered to replace Carrick.

Keiran McKenna, the former Ipswich Town manager and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler are also admired by the hierarchy, but sources have told ESPN that club bosses that United's current situation requires a manager with more experience.

Pochettino has extensive Premier League experience after spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has been considered for the United job before in 2018, 2022 and 2024.

articles.headline: How Harry Kane rose to win Ballon d'Or and became an England legend
articles.description: Harry Kane went from overlooked youngster to Ballon d'Or winner. Now he's about to become England's record appearance-holder -- and possibly their greatest-ever player.
articles.body:
Another week, another landmark moment for Harry Kane. Life is like that right now for the England captain, who will become his country's all-time record appearance-maker when leading out the Three Lions against Croatia on Thursday.

It completes a remarkable fortnight for Kane, 33, after he won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time and signed a new contract with Bayern Munich through to 2029. He is now one of the highest-paid players in Europe, at more than €30 million per year.

Surpassing Peter Shilton's 125-cap England record felt almost impossible for more than three decades, especially for an outfield player. Wayne Rooney reached 120, David Beckham 115, Steven Gerrard 114 and Ashley Cole 107, but Kane will go clear on his own with years still ahead of him.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

- Why Messi won't be 'do a Wrexham' as owner of non-league Cornellà

England's goal-scoring record appeared a similarly difficult climb. Sir Bobby Charlton's tally of 49 stood for 45 years before Rooney reached the half-century in 2015 and later ended on 53. Kane is on a remarkable 91 -- and counting.

He has captained England more often than any other player in history, leading England to back-to-back European Championship finals and a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, the men's national team's best placing since their sole 1966 triumph.

The only thing missing is a major international trophy, something he willingly admits he would trade every individual accolade to have. But Kane's case for becoming England's greatest-ever player grows with each passing season.

After ending his 19-year association with Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur, Kane joined Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich for €120 million in August 2023. In March of that year, Bayern appointed Thomas Tuchel as manager. Former sporting director Hasan Salihamidžić has publicly claimed the club decided on Kane as their top summer target around a month later having first considered him in late 2021.

"He took convincing, but don't forget Bayern Munich is a huge club with a big reputation," Tuchel, now Kane's manager with England, told ESPN. "The prospect of winning titles, the prospect of competing in the Champions League every year, quarterfinals, semifinals, finals in basically all competitions gave us a good hand.

"But still, it is a big step for the English captain to step out of the Premier League and then the language is not easy. So it was a big step out of his comfort zone for Harry.

"In the end, with hindsight, because we are all smarter, it seems to have brought out the very, very best in him. He adapted so quickly, he became such an influential figure in such a big club. Full credit to him and his family. He took convincing, but we felt from the start it was possible."

articles.headline: Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi denies wanting to leave amid Atlético Madrid links
articles.description: Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.

The Spanish midfielder has logged only 100 minutes in seven league appearances for Arsenal this term, a far cry from last season, where he played in all 38 Premier League games to help the Gunners win the title, averaging 79 minutes per game.

"I realise the winter transfer window is coming up, and rumours may start to circulate," he told Marca while on international duty with Spain.

"I've also read that a move [to Atlético] might be on the cards, but that's far from the case. I haven't wasted any energy on it, nor have I got in touch with anyone. I haven't wasted any energy on external matters. I've got enough on my plate just trying to earn a place in the team, get some playing time and fight to win this Premier League title, which is looking so promising."

Arsenal are top of the Premier League, five points clear of nearest rivals Brighton.

Asked if he will continue at Arsenal until the end of the season, Zubimendi, whose contract runs until June 2030, said: "Yes, I hope so. I'm happy there. I'm happy in London."

A 2026 World Cup winner with Spain, Zubimendi believes the workload of last season that led to physical fatigue, has affected his performances.

"I played an enormous number of minutes [last season], and, to be honest, I was tired," he said. "There were other factors, too, but the physical aspect could very well have been one of them."

Asked if he has considered seeking psychological help to deal with this bad patch, Zubimendi said: "I've thought about it and wouldn't rule it out, but for now, I haven't gone down that path.

"I'm well, I'm calm and happy with how I'm handling this situation. It's something I'd never experienced before, and I think you learn from situations like this too. What's more, it's at times like this that you need the people around you the most, and they're there for you."

Zubimendi, 27, is focusing on the positives.

"When you've been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to playing less, I'm managing to see the bright side," he said. "I think everything comes and goes; just as the opposite happened to me last year and I played practically every minute, things can change very quickly."

Zubimendi admits he was warned by Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta that the he would face competition for playing time with the arrival of midfielder Bruno Guimarães.

"I spoke to Mikel [Arteta] at the start of the season," Zubimendi said.

articles.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
articles.description: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
articles.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.
